name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis, including an in-driver taste-funnel explore state and design-ratification state) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each `--via loop`; /spec:design, /spec:build, and /spec:review remain each stage's direct entry, spec-build-driver.js and spec-review-driver.js stepped: admission, wave derivation, gate resolution, red-check, the final gate, scope-reconcile, legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros, and verdict derived by verdict.js, with test-author dispatch, per-wave worker dispatch, repair, reviewer dispatch, and dispositions held by the session) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.61.0 — mocks provenance ledger + the question gate's product-stage exemption (specs/20260902/06-mocks-provenance-ledger.md): a markdown ledger, `design/mocks/ledger.md`, two fixed-column tables (Assumptions, Misunderstandings) parsed by `spec/scripts/lib/mocks-ledger.js` (`parseLedger`, `gateVerdict`, `countsLine`, `appendAssumption`, `appendCatch`, `setStatus` — the one writer); every enum cell is one fixed word (kind `product|process`, tag `said-by-user|ratified-doc|inferred|invented`, status `open|confirmed|overridden|decided` + optional date). A ledger is blocked when any `product` row is `invented` (not `overridden`) or `inferred` + `open`; `ratified-doc` and `process` rows never block. `question-style-gate.js` gains a product-stage exemption: while `design/mocks/status.json` is not `APPROVED` or `.claude/genesis/status.json` has no `handoff`, a `derive` verdict is treated as `pass` (`rewrite` and tier 1 unchanged), and the judge prompt now states that a document citing a subject is never the user deciding it. New `spec/doctrine/mocks.md` (`spec-paths shared-mocks`) carries the ledger grammar; core § Question Style gains the one-sentence rule. Deviation: target version 7.60.0 was already taken by a concurrent fix, bumped to the next free minor 7.61.0 (rules § Gotchas). 7.60.0 — disposition-pool unit fix (direct fix, core § Incident Policy): a `leg:<name>` disposition covers that leg’s WHOLE finding count. `spec-review-driver.js --mark dispositions` weighs each leg entry by the same count `verdict.js` sums into legFindings (both now require `lib/leg-findings.js`, the one derivation — reconcile outOfPlan, ac-matrix uncovered, skip-reconcile skipped minus sanctioned, promise-sweep orphans, else 1), prints `count=N` per leg in the DISPOSITIONS step body, and names the leg weight when the tally check refuses. Before: the driver counted one per entry while the verdict counted findings, so one waived reconcile leg with outOfPlan:5 accepted `--waived 1`, derived HARD_FINDINGS forever, and refused `--waived 5` (prax specs/20260902/02-freeze-record.review/). Rejected: per-file refs (changes the disposer contract). Pinned by tests/review/disposer-gate.test.js. 7.59.0 — manifest-stamped review scope (specs/20260902/05-manifest-stamped-scope.md): `review-legs.js` stamps every row it appends with `scope: "full"|"fix-delta"` (its own writer only; `ac-matrix.js`/`promise-sweep.js` rows are unchanged); `verdict.js` derives the review profile's required-leg set from those manifest rows (carriers must agree; none means `full`; disagreement or a value outside the enum invalidates the manifest) and never from the reviewer's return, printing one stderr diagnostic naming the missing legs or the invalid row on `UNVERIFIED`; the review-profile ledger row and retained artifact carry that same manifest-derived `scope` on every row, hard-stop rows included. `spec-review-driver.js --mark dispositions` now refuses (exit 2, no write) when the pass is `UNVERIFIED`, printing the verdict diagnostic plus the sidecar path and the bare re-run command — dispositions cannot cure missing evidence. The reviewer return contract drops `scope`: `spec/commands/review.md` and `spec/agents/reviewer.md` now name `{verdict, survivors, killed, reviewerCount, tokens}`; a return that still carries `scope` is accepted and the key ignored.
